language.howToChooseYourGradeIntro: Our curriculum Grades K to 6 corresponds with ages:
language.howToChooseYourGradeContent:
It’s very important children start at the right level, have fun in learning and work at their own pace. Please help the children selecting the level that is not too easy, but also not too difficult for them. There are two ways to do this.

  • You can either check the learning goals yourself to determine the correct level for your child(ren).
  • Or you can let the child take several lessons to determine his or her level. For example, if your child has the age of 6, please let him or her take one lesson in grade K, one lesson in grade 1, and one lesson in grade 2 to determine at which level he or she is.

dialog.text: Hello, I am Tim.
Hello Sailor! My name is Pablo. Welcome to my cruise ship! We are in the beautiful port of Buenos Aires in Argentina, on the continent of South-America. As you can see, it is nice and sunny today.
Today I will teach you about heat, temperature and thermometers.
Come on! I will show you!
First, let's start with the difference between heat and temperature, because they are definitely not the same thing! Heat is something we can feel.
Think about rays of sunshine on your face, or the heat of a candle flame. You can feel the warmth from these objects.
However, we do not know how warm it is exactly. If we want to know that, we have to measure the heat. We call this, measuring the temperature.
We cannot feel temperature. Temperature is a measuring standard of the warmth or coldness of an object or substance.
Measuring temperature is a bit like checking your weight with a scale or finding out how tall you are with a measuring tape.
Oh, and you can also measure your body temperature with a thermometer.
Ok, let's go sailor!

Great job, Sailor! Now that you understand the gap between heat and temperature, let's dive into how hot and cold things can affect how warm or cool it feels!
Let's have some fun predicting what happens to a thermometer in different situations! Imagine a snowy day - it's really cold, so the temperature on the thermometer goes down.
Now, think about making tea by heating up water - it gets hot, so the temperature on the thermometer goes up.
Now, let's play a game! I'll show you pictures, and you drag them to the right thermometer. If it's hot, place it by the red one; if it's cold, put it by the blue one.
